sentences.text: Case of complainant in brief is that the complainant had purchased plot no.1, 2 and 3 from co-accused Tara Chand by notarized agreement, but original notarized agreement of plot no.3 was lost.
Therefore, applicant no.1/ accused Smt. Vandana Dixit after making photocopy of notarized agreement of plot no.3, replaced the name of complainant with her name by the aid of co- accused Prakash.
Thereby, the applicants and co-accused persons committed forgery and cheating against the complainant.
The complainant filed written complaint to the police but all went in vain.
Therefore, the complainant filed a complaint before JMFC, Indore, u/s 420, 467, 468 and 120-B of IPC against the accused persons.
3. Learned counsel for the applicants/accused persons submits that, applicants have not committed the offence and have falsely been implicated in the case.
After taking cognizance, arrest warrant has been issued, therefore, the applicants have apprehension of arrest, therefore, it is prayed that the applicants be granted anticipatory bail.
4. On other hand learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the application of the applicants and prayed for its rejection.
5. Counsel for the non-applicant/ complainant has filed no objection application and pleaded that complainant has no objection if the applicants granted anticipatory bail.

5. Having heard learned counsels for the parties, perused the case-diary also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in view of this court, it is a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicants.
Resultantly, without commenting upon the merits, applications for anticipatory bail are allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant - VANDANA DIXIT and HARISHANKAR DIXIT shall be released on bail upon their furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only)each with separate sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for their appearance before the Trial Court on all dates and for complying with the conditions enumerated in sub-section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
7. M.Cr.C. stands disposed of, accordingly.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
